title: I can't find any syntax to allow me to specify an index and a limit for DELETE

comments.text:
Description:
When deleting rows from a large table, I've found that I can improve the performance of my query significantly by specifying an index to use. However I also want to limit the deleting in order to limit the resources used by the clean up process.

How to repeat:
Attempt to run a query that both specifies index hints and a limit.

Suggested fix:
Either allow indexes to be specified in the single table delete or allow limit to be used in certain versions of the multi table delete.

Either:
DELETE r.* FROM audit_reference r USE INDEX(`organisation_created`) WHERE created < '2018-03-02 10:35:55.68' LIMIT 100000

Or:
DELETE FROM audit_reference USE INDEX(`organisation_created`) WHERE created < '2018-03-02 10:35:55.68' LIMIT 100000

Hello Matthew,

Thank you for the bug report.

Please note that MySQL uses indexes to find the rows matching a WHERE clause quickly. 
For more info please see https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/mysql-indexes.html

You can use DELETE statement with LIMIT. Please see here https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/delete.html

Regards,
Ashwini Patil
